messages:
maya-support: Escalation from Org org-762 — customer reports sustained 429s + high p50 latency on Dedicated Platinum pool for the last 40m. They say requests are being throttled even though their reserved capacity should cover. Example response headers from failed requests attached by customer:

sam-cust-success: (pasted) curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-redwood-ORG-762" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Org: org-762" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd/platinum-7b","input":"hi"}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 10
X-Redwood-Pool: standard-pool-2
X-Request-Id: req-202603170945-9f2b

maya-support: Customer insists pool assignment should be dedicated-platinum-1. They attached a control-plane debug snippet where routing decision says "matched policy: platinum-v1" then later logs show "selected pool: standard-pool-2 (fallback)". They suspect routing fallback misfired.

luke-sre: Can you drop the exact control-plane logs + request id? I want the tracing link. Also: did this start after the control-plane deploy this morning? deploy-bot: deploy control-plane v3.14.0 -> prod @ 2026-03-17T09:05Z :rocket: (rolled out to 4 regions)

sam-cust-success: Pasted logs (redacted):
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] route-eval: req=req-202603170945-9f2b org=org-762 policy_matched=platinum-v1 rules=[tier:platinum,region:us-east]
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] pool-select: candidate_pools=[dedicated-platinum-1,dedicated-platinum-2] available=[dedicated-platinum-1] selected=standard-pool-2 fallback_reason=pool_disabled_in_cache
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] throttle: reason=throttled_by_pool_selected capacity=0/100
```

maya-support: Customer says dedicated-platinum-1 shows healthy in infra dashboard and has spare capacity. They see no incident on their end.

rachel-runtime: Noted. This looks like a control-plane decision path where the availability cache says pool disabled, then a fallback picks a default standard pool. Hypothesis: the new routing change that simplified rule matching may be marking pools unavailable when the pool tagset includes an alias.

luke-sre: Quick repro we tried locally: call API with org header + spoofed org rate and inspect x-redwood-pool header. We got the same fallback when the org policy included a trailing space in tier label (e.g., "platinum "), which the new matcher normalizes differently. Repro command:
```
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-redwood-ORG-762" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Org: org-762" \
  -H "X-Feature-Flag: controlplane-v3.14.0" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response headers show: X-Redwood-Pool: standard-pool-2

rachel-runtime: If that's true the normalizer can produce a mismatch: policy says "platinum" but cache keys used to be stored without trimming when pools were registered. New matcher trims which causes looking up an exact key to fail -> pool seen as unavailable -> fallback. That fits logs.

maya-support: Customer impact: 20% of requests hitting fallback for the last 40m, p50 latency doubled, repeated 429s. Billing/usage still counts but not honoring reserved throughput. They want rollback or workaround.

rachel-runtime: Short-term mitigation: we can apply a routing override for org-762 to pin to dedicated-platinum-1 until fix. Command for ops: 
```
redwoodctl routing override set --org org-762 --pool dedicated-platinum-1 --expires-in 2h --reason "support emergency"
```
I can also push a hotfix to the control-plane routing to make cache lookups tolerant to trimmed/untouched keys (small change). Will need a 30-min canary then prod.

luke-sre: I'll apply the override now and add a metric alert for any other orgs that hit fallback > 5% in 10m.

maya-support: Applied override and notified customer. They confirm immediate improvement in last 2 minutes, seeing responses coming from dedicated-platinum-1 and 429s subsiding :thumbsup:.

rachel-runtime: Triage notes for engineering: suspected regression introduced in PR #4127 (routing: normalize-tier-keys). Repro steps included above. Patch plan: make lookup tolerant by checking both trimmed and original keys, add unit tests for trailing whitespace and alias mapping, and add integration test hitting live cache. ETA for hotfix: 2h to merge + 30m canary.

sam-cust-success: Customer wants a postmortem and confirmation that billing/usage will be reconciled if they lost reserved capacity. Assigning billing engagement.

luke-sre: Creating incident ticket INC-2026-03017 and alert runbook updated. Will follow up with rollback if hotfix causes regressions.

rachel-runtime: I'll post PR link when open and ping eng-oncall. For now, override is in place and metrics look good. :eyes:

maya-support: Thanks team. I'll close the escalated ticket once we have hotfix merged or rollback decision.

infra-bot: [metric] fallback_rate_org_org-762: 0.9% (was 21% 15m ago)

deploy-bot: deployment control-plane v3.14.1 scheduled (hotfix) -> will canary in 10m

rachel-runtime: Hotfix PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/runtime/+/PR-4189 (adds tolerant lookup + tests). Canaries green at 10m. Planning prod push in 20m.

maya-support: Customer notified of temporary fix and hotfix timeline. Closing loop when prod push is complete.
